statement_en: Let $P =\begin{pmatrix}0,1\\0,0\end{pmatrix}$ and $Q =\begin{pmatrix}0,0\\0,1\end{pmatrix}$. Then $$PQ=\begin{pmatrix}0,1\\0,0\end{pmatrix},\quad QP=\begin{pmatrix}0,0\\0,0\end{pmatrix}.$$ The characteristic polynomials of $PQ$ and $QP$ are both $x^2$. However, one minimal polynomial is $x^2$ and the other is $x$.

import Mathlib

open Matrix Polynomial

theorem matrix_products_charpoly_minpoly_example :
    let P : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℚ := !![0, 1; 0, 0]
    let Q : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℚ := !![0, 0; 0, 1]
    P ⬝ Q = !![0, 1; 0, 0] ∧
      Q ⬝ P = !![0, 0; 0, 0] ∧
      Matrix.charpoly (P ⬝ Q) = (X : Polynomial ℚ) ^ 2 ∧
      Matrix.charpoly (Q ⬝ P) = (X : Polynomial ℚ) ^ 2 ∧
      minpoly ℚ (P ⬝ Q) = (X : Polynomial ℚ) ^ 2 ∧
      minpoly ℚ (Q ⬝ P) = (X : Polynomial ℚ) := by
